subject: Hotpath bleed + reservation erosion — urgent burst runway & exec ask
messages:
From: BrightCore Ops <ops@brightcore.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: urgent: p95 latency up 3x and 502 rate climbing on dedicated pool

Irene / Aditya —

We're seeing a sustained p95 increase from ~180ms to ~620ms across our inference endpoints tied to the dedicated GPU pool (reserved). Error rate (502/5xx) has climbed to ~4.8% over the last 40m. Throughput is also degraded: our reserved qps slices are returning throttled responses and retries are amplifying queueing. Impact: customer-facing features are timing out and page load times are spiking.

Key numbers from our side:
- p50: 120ms -> 170ms
- p95: 180ms -> 620ms
- 5xx rate: 0.2% -> 4.8%
- Effective throughput (tokens/sec): down ~38% vs baseline

We've attached a heap/profile snapshot and a short runbook excerpt. Need immediate help to understand whether this is a noisy neighbor on the pool or a failing kernel path. Do you have any immediate mitigation (model fallback, reserve burst, route-by-policy) we should try?

Samir Patel
SRE, BrightCore AI

Attachment: heap_profile.tar.gz (tar.gz)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: BrightCore Ops <ops@brightcore.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: urgent: p95 latency up 3x and 502 rate climbing on dedicated pool

Samir — thanks for the data and the snapshot. I'm pulling Eng and Network in now; copying Vivek because this hits reserved capacity and may need exec approval for burst credits. Initial asks and quick mitigations we can try in parallel:

1) Route-by-policy: divert 30% of BrightCore traffic to the compatible lower-cost model-quant variant (same family, 8-bit quant) for 20 minutes to reduce KV cache pressure. Minimal quality delta expected.
2) Short-term burst: approve a 2-hour reserved burst (warm GPUs) while we triage. Vivek — can we authorize?
3) KV-cache inspection: Aditya, can you check hot-key eviction and prefix cache hit rates in the last 60m? If the KV cache is thrashing that would explain headroom erosion.
4) Canary config: add tighter timeouts and increase priority for small payloads to reduce head-of-line blocking.

I'll stand up an ops bridge in 10 minutes and attach the runbook.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, BrightCore Ops <ops@brightcore.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: urgent: p95 latency up 3x and 502 rate climbing on dedicated pool

I've pulled the metrics. Quick findings:
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 94% -> 61% starting ~08:45 PST. Eviction rate spiked concurrent with an increase in long-context requests from a burst window.
- One worker node has a driver-level retry loop logged; we see elevated GPU queue depth on node gpu-pool-17.
- Model kernel timings show a 12-16% increase on attention kernel for sequence lengths > 1024.

Immediate actions taken:
- Force-evict stale prefixes for BrightCore's namespace to free KV entries (manual patch applied).
- Rebalanced a small fraction (10%) of BrightCore traffic to model-quant-8b.
- Isolated gpu-pool-17 and draining for deeper logs; moving traffic off that node now.

Effect so far: p95 reduced to ~420ms and 5xx to ~2.1% after the rebalancing and eviction — still not back to baseline.

Notes: if we can't recover to baseline within 60-90m, ask for 2-hour burst continuation + procurement loop for extra reserved slices. Also recommend running a short recompile to pick optimized kernels for long sequences — that will take ~45m.

— Aditya
Senior SWE, Serving Runtime
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, BrightCore Ops <ops@brightcore.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: urgent: p95 latency up 3x and 502 rate climbing on dedicated pool

Irene / team —

I've approved an immediate 2-hour burst window from central reserved capacity to cover BrightCore while SRE/Eng triage. Procurement: Marissa, please flag for potential credit/contract adjustment; Samir, we'll coordinate the formal procurement ask after stabilization.

Operational plan (next 6 hours):
- 0-30m: continue traffic shed to model-quant-8b and keep draining gpu-pool-17.
- 30-90m: run kernel recompile for long-seq paths; monitor p95 and 5xx.
- 90-240m: if improvement < 75% of baseline, initiate temporary reserved slice add (30% of current reservation) and propose SLA credit to BrightCore for partial remediation.

Please capture any customer requests for credits / formal compensation and loop me in. I'm scheduling a 4pm PT exec sync if we need cross-functional approval to extend burst beyond 2h.

— Vivek
VP, Customer Success Operations
From: BrightCore Ops <ops@brightcore.ai>

Subject: Re: Hotpath bleed + reservation erosion — urgent burst runway & exec ask

Team —

Thanks for the fast response and the temporary burst. Update from our side: the mitigation steps helped materially — p95 now oscillates between 160-220ms on most endpoints, and 5xx is down to 0.6% aggregated. We saw one regression window when long-context requests spiked again; the kernel recompile appears to have helped reduce the long-tail.

Requests moving forward:
- Can we convert the temporary burst into an interim reserved slice for the remainder of the month while we renegotiate forecast? BrightCore has a forecast revision arriving next week; we need avoidance of repeated headroom erosion during our peak windows.
- Please share the runbook excerpt you referenced and any logs that explain the root cause (eviction + long-seq compounding). We'll include those in our postmortem with product.

Appreciate the exec sync offer — Samir, if you're available, we'd like to join the 4pm PT slot tomorrow.

Samir Patel
SRE, BrightCore AI
